0 Black Narrows Two players take turns adding black stones to an initially empty, rectangular grid, one stone per turn. After your placement, there must be an orthogonally interconnected path of unoccupied points, of length at least 1, connecting every pair of stones. The last player to place a stone wins. In other words, if you don't have an available placement on your turn, you lose. Black Narrows is known in combinatorial game theory language as an impartial game.
